Analysis: Both hypotheses propose that inhibiting ENTPD2 can reduce MDSC-mediated immunosuppression and thereby improve checkpoint inhibitor efficacy in HCC. Hypothesis 1 introduces a novel element by specifically focusing on the hypoxic microenvironment in HCC, which adds a layer of mechanistic complexity and novelty. However, this same complexity poses challenges in experimental validation and may introduce additional safety concerns related to the specific hypoxic context. Hypothesis 2, while slightly more conventional by not restricting itself to hypoxic conditions, clearly outlines the restoration of cytotoxic T cell activity and benefits from a simpler, more straightforward design that is likely easier to test and translate clinically. Considering all criteria—novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety—Hypothesis 2 strikes a better balance between innovative therapeutic insight and pragmatic experimental design.
